reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) shows that trace interstitials promote phase segregation and matrix softening during aging, but it does not provide any data on grain-boundary segregation, reduced cohesion, or intergranular fracture. The key premises linking impurities to embrittlement are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Trace oxygen and nitrogen in single-phase HEAs segregate to grain boundaries during high-temperature aging
This segregation forms impurity-rich zones or incipient nano-precipitates at grain boundaries
These grain-boundary features reduce cohesive strength and cause brittle intergranular fracture
Reducing impurity levels will suppress this embrittlement and preserve toughness
The Ti-V-Nb-Ta alloy system is a valid model for this mechanism
